title: Underdog Accused of Stealing Model Weights and AI Engine from Startups
summary:
Industry critics claim the Ternary model developed by AI startup Underdog is a modified version of PrismML's Bonsai 2 with its original attribution removed. The allegations, echoed by engineer Vikhyat K, suggest the company also took its inference engine, known as Splash, from Inco AI to achieve its performance metrics. These claims of misappropriated model weights and software follow the debut of Underdog's on-device AI assistant.

Underdog was launched by founder Sigil Wen with financial backing from a16z, Khosla Ventures, Hummingbird, and the Anthology fund, which includes Anthropic and Menlo Ventures. Wen started the company after testing the cyber capabilities of frontier models led him to move personal data from cloud data centers to local hardware. The company operates under "Underdog's Law," asserting that the latest frontier intelligence reaches consumer devices within 6 months of release.

selectedTweets.text:
.@0xSigil reveals testing frontier AI's cyber capabilities scared him enough to start moving his personal data off data centers and onto his own devices:

"There is going to be a radical reformation of the economy as businesses and the economy shift to serving agents as one of its newest users on the internet, especially as humans trust AIs more to act on their behalf."

"We were working on agents that could run on long horizon harnesses, and we were also testing different frontier models, and it was just really scarily apparent just how good at cyber they were."

"It was really clear to me that, oh my God, Mythos class models are open source now. I think that really led to me wanting to build Underdog for myself."

"I wanna bring my data onto my devices, off of data centers, which are some of the biggest targets."
